neighbours.label: In English text, the word just before an expected ringing or whistling sound verb (e.g. 'the alarm clock began to' before 'ring', 'your phone' before 'rings', 'the kettle began to' before 'whistle'), and the first piece 'par' of a body part being physically paralysed. Also fires on 'lé' in French 'blessés légers'. Quiet for predictable words in general, when nothing is about to ring or whistle (the truck began to move), for figurative paralysis (a committee paralysed by debate), and for ringing in other languages.
neighbours.short: just before an expected ring/whistle, or 'par' of paralysed
fire: At exactly six in the morning the alarm clock began to ring.
I was halfway through my sentence when your phone rings again.
She set the kettle on the stove, and soon the kettle began to whistle.
The bell over the shop door rang as the customer walked in.
We were sitting down to dinner when the doorbell started to ring.
The referee lifted the whistle to his lips and blew a sharp whistle.
As the train approached the crossing, it let out a long whistle.
quiet: She lit the candles on the cake and everyone sang happy birthday.
At exactly six in the morning the delivery truck began to move.
I was halfway through my sentence when your brother walks in again.
She set the pot on the stove, and soon the water began to boil.
The door of the shop opened as the customer walked in.
We were sitting down to dinner when the lights started to flicker.
The referee raised his hand and pointed toward the penalty spot.
As the train approached the crossing, it slowly began to brake.

predictions: Blind-authored test (label-only second author). Expect the ring/whistle setups to fire and the move/boil/flicker twins to stay quiet; the shop-bell and train-whistle items are less certain.
